title: Psychiatrist Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay Using a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to calculate a psychiatrist salary from hourly rates using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes award rates, tax, and superannuation estimates.
salarySummary: Using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Health Professionals Award, a Level 4 health professional earns $65.77 per hour, equating to an annual salary of about $130,000 for 38 hours per week. However, psychiatrists typically earn above award rates.

faqs.a: The Jobs and Skills Australia profile for psychiatrists does not provide median earnings due to high standard error. faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly psychiatrist rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by 38 (standard full-time hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year). For example, $60/hour × 38 × 52 = $118,560 gross per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a psychiatrist under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award, a Level 4 health professional earns $65.77 per hour. However, psychiatrists are medical practitioners and may be covered by a different award or enterprise agreement with higher rates. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Psychiatrist Salary Calculations

When evaluating a psychiatrist salary, it's common to start with an hourly rate and convert it to an annual figure. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, as defined in many modern awards including the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020. The annual gross pay is calculated by multiplying the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week and then by 52 weeks.

For example, if a psychiatrist earns $60 per hour, the annual gross salary would be $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates or allowances. It's a useful baseline for comparing job offers.

### Award Rates and Minimum Pay

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets minimum rates for health professionals under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award. For a Health Professional employee at Level 4, the minimum hourly rate is $65.77. However, psychiatrists are medical practitioners and are typically covered by the Medical Practitioners Award 2020 or enterprise agreements, which often provide higher rates. The award rates serve as a floor; actual psychiatrist salaries are usually above these minimums.

### Using ABS Data for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This translates to an annual salary of approximately $108,352 ($2,083.70 × 52). While this is an average across all occupations, it provides a benchmark. For psychiatrists, the Jobs and Skills Australia profile notes that median weekly earnings are not available due to high standard error. This means precise national averages for psychiatrist pay are not published, but individual job advertisements and enterprise agreements can give more specific figures.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a $60/hour psychiatrist, weekly pay is $2,280, so fortnightly is $4,560. This is helpful for budgeting.

### Tax and Superannuation

From the annual gross salary, you need to consider tax and super. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) resident tax rates for 2026-27 are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low incomes). For a $118,560 salary, the tax would be approximately $27,000 plus Medicare, leaving around $89,000 after tax (estimate).

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For $118,560, that's an extra $14,227.20 contributed to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual psychiatrist, you are entitled to a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. For example, a casual health professional at Level 1 would get $26.97 + 25% = $33.71 per hour. However, psychiatrists are rarely casual; most are permanent employees.

### Internal Resources

For more detailed calculations, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to convert any rate. You can also explore [job pay](/topics/job-pay) for occupation-specific guides.

## Conclusion

Calculating a psychiatrist salary from an hourly rate involves a simple formula: hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks. While precise national averages for psychiatrists are not available from the provided data, you can use award rates and ABS averages as reference points. Always check your specific award or contract for exact pay conditions.
